key_insight: Drilled-to-bossed geometry enhanced AA2024-T351 friction-weld strength, while an ensemble residual network predicted ultimate tensile strength with R² ≈ 0.81.
engineering_relevance: Combining mechanical interlocking with data-driven prediction could support stronger lightweight aluminium joints for aerospace and automotive applications.
method: Tested direct drive friction welding on a customized engine lathe using an L18 orthogonal experimental design.
Varied friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, faying geometry, and friction time.
Compared ensemble residual, compact attention, and adaptive multiscale networks for tensile-strength prediction.
evidence_signal: The reported optimum—30 MPa friction pressure, 70 MPa forging pressure, 2200 rpm, drilled-to-bossed geometry, and 4 min friction time—achieved 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify predictive validation details; the limited L18 design warrants independent testing before generalizing the model or process settings.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
